A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SciFlow-Bench and support a complete comparison of text, figures, tables, and mathematical content. Appendices A–D match in both text and rendered appearance, shifting from pages 11–17 to pages 13–19.

before.justification: v1 reports original six-generator benchmark results, human verification of 100 source figures, parser ablations, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those results and adds human-referenced validation on 90 generated diagrams and a structured-versus-naive prompt ablation.

M1.justification: The proposed planning, perception, fusion, and structural-reasoning pipeline remains unchanged, as do its matching and scoring procedures. The new prompt ablation tests the existing planning layer without revising the proposed method.

E1.justification: The 500-instance, five-domain benchmark remains unchanged. New Section 4.3 extends human-referenced parser validation from source-paper figures to generated diagrams from Graphviz, Qwen-Image, and Gemini 3 Pro Image, adding a generated-image validation scenario.

E2.justification: v2 Table 6 introduces Naive Prompt, retaining only the method description, as a comparator to the planning layer's Structured Prompt. The six generator baselines and existing parser-ablation variants remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 90-image human-reference audit with 30 images per generator and the existing node/edge precision, recall, and F1 protocol. It also adds a controlled structured-versus-naive prompt comparison while holding the dataset, generation settings, and inverse-parsing protocol fixed. Existing benchmark settings are retained.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 adds quantitative testing of parser reliability on generated-image distributions, and Section 5.3 adds planning-layer prompt ablation across all six generators. These substantially expand validation beyond the retained perception-component ablations and qualitative analyses. Appendix D's examples are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without adding repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new audit's sample counts describe evaluated images, not repeated runs.

E6.justification: Two substantive sets of results are added. Table 2 reports HMAS Node/Edge F1 of 0.96/0.89 on Graphviz, 0.87/0.68 on Qwen-Image, and 0.90/0.70 on Gemini 3 Pro Image. Table 6 adds naive-prompt results across six generators; Gemini 3 Pro Image scores 0.051 graph-level and 0.176 overall, versus 0.116 and 0.311 under structured prompts. Original annotation, leaderboard, and perception-ablation values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The graph formulation, semantic and path-aware matching definitions, and aggregation rules in Section 3 and Appendix A remain unchanged. No mathematical derivation, theorem, or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a 500-instance structure-first benchmark, round-trip evaluation through inverse parsing, and a gap between visual fidelity and structural recoverability. New experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the generated-image audit as supporting evaluator stability and attributes remaining errors primarily to diagram ambiguity or structural collapse. It also argues that planning prevents an underspecified task. Existing limitations and appendix interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: A new first-page footnote supplies a SciFlow-Bench repository link, adding an access pointer. Appendix A's implementation and reproducibility descriptions remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish the linked repository's contents.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds SciGenBench and its Lin et al. (2026) reference, acknowledging evaluation of logical correctness and information utility while retaining the distinction concerning directed and hierarchical structure. Other cited works and the main research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized edits to related work, experimental setup, ablation discussion, and conclusion. It inserts Section 4.3, organizes the ablation discussion around perception and planning, and adds affiliations, a project-leader designation, and acknowledgments. The overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the generated-diagram reliability table and the structured/naive prompt table, moves Figure 3 to the following page, and reflows and renumbers existing material. Existing figures and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 partly closes a relevant validation gap by checking HMAS against human references on generated diagrams and adds controlled evidence for the planning layer's contribution. These strengthen the benchmark's empirical support. The gain remains limited: the audit covers three generators with 30 images each, reports no uncertainty, and does not establish the accompanying attribution of remaining errors primarily to the diagrams themselves.
